claims.source: Emerging evidence further demonstrates abnormalities of vlPFC in tight association with deficits in cognitive flexibility (Neubert et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2020; Zhan et al., 2021), suggesting that an elaborate delineation of its hard wiring would shed light on the underlying neuropathology of psychiatric disorders (Haber et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Neubert et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2020; and Zhan et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Histological neural tracing continues to be the most reliable way of survey for all myelinated axons in mammalian brains.
claims.source: Histological neural tracing has been historically utilized for circuit/pathway mapping and continues to be the most reliable way of survey for all myelinated axons in mammalian brains (Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018; Bienkowski et al., 2018), which has also been used as a gold standard to validate other modalities like diffusion tractography (Schmahmann et al., 2007; Donahue et al., 2016; Reveley et al., 2015; Mortazavi et al., 2018; Folloni et al., 2019; Dyrby et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018; and Bienkowski et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Histological neural tracing has been used as a gold standard to validate diffusion tractography.
claims.source: Histological neural tracing has been historically utilized for circuit/pathway mapping and continues to be the most reliable way of survey for all myelinated axons in mammalian brains (Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018; Bienkowski et al., 2018), which has also been used as a gold standard to validate other modalities like diffusion tractography (Schmahmann et al., 2007; Donahue et al., 2016; Reveley et al., 2015; Mortazavi et al., 2018; Folloni et al., 2019; Dyrby et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schmahmann et al., 2007; Donahue et al., 2016; Reveley et al., 2015; Mortazavi et al., 2018; Folloni et al., 2019; and Dyrby et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Diffusion tractography represents the only methodology capable of inferring the ensemble of anatomical connections in the living animal or human brain.
claims.source: Diffusion tractography, which has been developed in the 1990s to estimate the tissue microstructure by means of spatial encoding of water molecule movements (Basser et al., 1994), represents the only methodology capable of inferring the ensemble of anatomical connections in the living animal or human brain (Wedeen et al., 2012; Mori and Zhang, 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wedeen et al., 2012 and Mori and Zhang, 2006.

claims.claim: Diffusion tractography is an indirect observation with limited resolution and accuracy.
claims.source: But this technique is an indirect observation with limited resolution and accuracy, and its reliability of false negative and false positive findings remains to be fully validated in a 3D space (Donahue et al., 2016; Maier-Hein et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Donahue et al., 2016 and Maier-Hein et al., 2017.

claims.claim: The reliability of false negative and false positive findings in diffusion tractography remains to be fully validated in a 3D space.
claims.source: But this technique is an indirect observation with limited resolution and accuracy, and its reliability of false negative and false positive findings remains to be fully validated in a 3D space (Donahue et al., 2016; Maier-Hein et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Donahue et al., 2016 and Maier-Hein et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Viral-based techniques for targeting specific neuronal types in macaque brain have achieved remarkable success.
claims.source: Moreover, viral-based techniques for targeting specific neuronal types in macaque brain have achieved remarkable success (Han et al., 2009; Stauffer et al., 2016), which may furnish the requisite biological detail including excitatory and inhibitory in-/output to enrich structural network reconstructions for improved prediction of brain function (Suárez et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Han et al., 2009 and Stauffer et al., 2016.

claims.claim: It remains unclear what type of viral vector is suitable for long-range axonal fiber tracing.
claims.source: However, it remains unclear thus far what type of viral vector is suitable for long-range axonal fiber tracing (Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zeng, 2018 and Luo et al., 2018.

claims.claim: The IFOF supposedly connects the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex and medial orbitofrontal cortex to the occipital lobe through the ventral part of the external capsule.
claims.source: The IFOF first proposed in the early 19th century supposedly connects the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex and medial orbitofrontal cortex to the occipital lobe through the ventral part of the external capsule (Curran, 1909; Catani et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Curran, 1909 and Catani et al., 2002.

claims.claim: Micro-dissection and diffusion MRI tractography studies have confirmed the anatomy of the IFOF pathway.
claims.source: Micro-dissection and diffusion MRI tractography studies have recently confirmed the anatomy of this pathway (Sarubbo et al., 2019; Barrett et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sarubbo et al., 2019 and Barrett et al., 2020.

claims.claim: A number of axonal tracing studies have failed to reveal the IFOF in the macaque brain.
claims.source: Despite an abundance of functional evidence supporting a central role of occipito-frontal circuitry in cognition and sensory integration, a number of axonal tracing studies, which have been able to identify monosynaptic connections, have failed to reveal the IFOF in the macaque brain (Schmahmann et al., 2007; Schmahmann and Pandya, 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schmahmann et al., 2007 and Schmahmann and Pandya, 2006.

claims.claim: Sparse connections between frontal and occipital cortices in macaques were reported by other labs.
claims.source: By contrast, sparse connections between frontal and occipital cortices in macaques were reported by other labs (Gerbella et al., 2010; Markov et al., 2014), although they do not show whether these axons follow the course expected for the IFOF.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerbella et al., 2010 and Markov et al., 2014.

claims.claim: The study established a comprehensive brain-wide excitatory projectome of the vlPFC in macaque monkeys using viral-based genetic tracing in tandem with serial two-photon (STP) tomography.
claims.source: In the present study, we aim to establish a comprehensive brain-wide excitatory projectome of the vlPFC in macaque monkeys using viral-based genetic tracing in tandem with serial two-photon (STP) tomography (Figure 1A), a technique that has successfully achieved high-throughput fluorescence imaging of the entire mouse brain by integrating two-photon microscopy and tissue sectioning (Ragan et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the study's methodology and a citation to Ragan et al., 2012.

claims.claim: STP tomography has successfully achieved high-throughput fluorescence imaging of the entire mouse brain by integrating two-photon microscopy and tissue sectioning.
claims.source: In the present study, we aim to establish a comprehensive brain-wide excitatory projectome of the vlPFC in macaque monkeys using viral-based genetic tracing in tandem with serial two-photon (STP) tomography (Figure 1A), a technique that has successfully achieved high-throughput fluorescence imaging of the entire mouse brain by integrating two-photon microscopy and tissue sectioning (Ragan et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ragan et al., 2012.

claims.claim: The study performed ex vivo dMRI scans of the entire macaque brains using an ultra-high field (11.7T) MRI scanner.
claims.source: We also performed ex vivo dMRI scans of the entire macaque brains to track the axonal fiber tracts using an ultra-high field (11.7T) MRI scanner (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and Figure 1C showing the dMRI setup.

claims.claim: Five days after infection with VSV-ΔG, neuronal cell bodies in the cerebral cortex and mediodorsal (MD) thalamus were clearly labeled with GFP.
claims.source: Five days after infection with VSV-ΔG, the neuronal cell bodies in the cerebral cortex (Figure 2A and B) and mediodorsal (MD) thalamus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) were clearly labeled with GFP, although only proximal neurites were labeled with no long-range axonal fibers detected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: VSV-ΔG infection for five days resulted in only proximal neurites being labeled with no long-range axonal fibers detected.
claims.source: Five days after infection with VSV-ΔG, the neuronal cell bodies in the cerebral cortex (Figure 2A and B) and mediodorsal (MD) thalamus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) were clearly labeled with GFP, although only proximal neurites were labeled with no long-range axonal fibers detected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: When VSV-ΔG infection time was extended to about a month, widespread axon loss and neuronal cell death were observed.
claims.source: When the infection time was extended to about a month, we observed widespread axon loss and neuronal cell death (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-G.

claims.claim: Long-term-infected neurons with VSV-ΔG underwent morphological changes such as membrane blebbing, a key morphological change associated with the induction of apoptosis.
claims.source: The long-term-infected neurons underwent morphological changes such as membrane blebbing (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C), a key morphological change associated with the induction of apoptosis.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C, and established knowledge about membrane blebbing.

claims.claim: Local injection with VSV-ΔG mediated rapid and transient gene expression nearby the injection site.
claims.source: Local injection with VSV-ΔG mediated rapid and transient gene expression nearby the injection site, and an extension of infection time evidently caused fatal neurotoxicity.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations described in the text.

claims.claim: An extension of VSV-ΔG infection time evidently caused fatal neurotoxicity.
claims.source: Local injection with VSV-ΔG mediated rapid and transient gene expression nearby the injection site, and an extension of infection time evidently caused fatal neurotoxicity.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations described in the text.

claims.claim: Lenti-Ubic-GFP exhibited stable expression in the cell soma even after 9 months.
claims.source: Lenti-Ubic-GFP exhibited stable expression in the cell soma even after 9 months (Figure 2C and D), despite sparse labeling of GFP positive axons (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 2C and D.

claims.claim: Lenti-Ubic-GFP resulted in sparse labeling of GFP positive axons.
claims.source: Lenti-Ubic-GFP exhibited stable expression in the cell soma even after 9 months (Figure 2C and D), despite sparse labeling of GFP positive axons (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Six weeks after AAV2/9-CaMKIIa-Tau-GFP was injected into the premotor cortex or MD thalamus, axonal fiber bundles like anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC) were clearly visualized over several centimeters.
claims.source: By contrast, 6 weeks after AAV2/9-CaMKIIa-Tau-GFP was injected into the premotor cortex (Figure 2E-G) or MD thalamus (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), axonal fiber bundles like anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC) (Figure 2G) were clearly visualized over several centimeters.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 2E-G, Figure 2—figure supplement 4, and Figure 2G.

claims.claim: AAV-infected cells were positive for the neuronal specific marker NeuN, but negative for astrocyte specific marker GFAP.
claims.source: The AAV-infected cells were positive for the neuronal specific marker NeuN, but negative for astrocyte specific marker GFAP (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claims.claim: The signal intensity of most Tau-GFP labeled axons was consistently higher than that of mCherry labeled axons.
claims.source: As a validation test, AAV2/9 construct encoding mCherry was co-injected with AAV2/9 construct encoding Tau-GFP into the premotor cortex. And we found that the signal intensity of most Tau-GFP labeled axons was consistently higher than that of mCherry labeled axons (Figure 2—figure supplement 6A-D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 6A-D.

claims.claim: The density of axonal fibers labeled by AAV2/9 was significantly higher than by Lentivirus and VSV-ΔG.
claims.source: The density of axonal fibers labeled by AAV2/9 (Figure 2—figure supplement 7C) was significantly higher (P < 0.001, Figure 2—figure supplement 7D) than by Lentivirus (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B) and VSV-ΔG (Figure 2—figure supplement 7A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, statistical analysis (P < 0.001), and references to Figure 2—figure supplement 7A-D.

claims.claim: Axons labeled by lentivirus were significantly denser than by VSV-ΔG distant from the injection site.
claims.source: Axons labeled by lentivirus (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B) were also significantly denser (P < 0.01, Figure 2—figure supplement 7D) than by VSV-ΔG (Figure 2—figure supplement 7A) distant from the injection site.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, statistical analysis (P < 0.01), and references to Figure 2—figure supplement 7A, B, and D.

claims.claim: AAV2/9 encoding Tau-GFP under the control of excitatory promoter CaMKIIa was determined as an anterograde tracer for mapping the excitatory projectome of vlPFC.
claims.source: AAV2/9 encoding Tau-GFP under the control of excitatory promoter CaMKIIa was determined as an anterograde tracer for mapping the excitatory projectome of vlPFC.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental design and methodology described in the text.

claims.claim: The injection site in vlPFC, including area 45, 12 l, and 44, was precisely located in cortical gray matter.
claims.source: The injection site in vlPFC, validated by STP images, including area 45, 12 l, and 44, was precisely located in cortical gray matter (Figure 4A-D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4A-D.

claims.claim: GFP-positive neurons in the injection site were observed positive for CaMkIIa and negative for GABA, indicating that the AAV labeled neurons were glutamate excitatory neurons.
claims.source: To identify the cell type specificity of Tau-GFP gene expression driven by the CaMKII-α promoter, immunofluorescent staining was performed with antibodies against the excitatory neuron specific marker CaMKII-α and the inhibitory neuron-specific neurotransmitter GABA. GFP-positive neurons in the injection site were observed positive for CaMkIIa (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C) and negative for GABA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F), indicating that the AAV labeled neurons were glutamate excitatory neurons.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-F.

claims.claim: GFP-labeled projecting axons from vlPFC largely encompassed the anterior part of the brain including the frontal lobe, temporal lobe, limbic regions, insular, and some subcortical regions, but no labeled axons were found in the occipital lobe.
claims.source: The GFP-labeled projecting axons largely encompassed the anterior part of the brain including the frontal lobe, temporal lobe, limbic regions, insular, and some subcortical regions, but no labeled axons were found in the occipital lobe (Figure 3A–C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 3A–C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Within the frontal lobe, GFP-labeled projecting axons were markedly dense in the OFC, rostrally distributed in area 12 m, 12o, 11 l, 13 l, and 13 m.
claims.source: Within the frontal lobe, GFP-labeled projecting axons were markedly dense in the OFC, rostrally distributed in area 12 m (Figure 4E, F and G), 12o (Figure 4E), 11 l (Figure 4E, H and I), 13 l (Figure 4E), and 13 m (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4E-I.

claims.claim: The 12 m received strongest innervation from vlPFC relative to other OFC subregions.
claims.source: The 12 m received strongest innervation from vlPFC relative to other OFC subregions (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Axonal projections from vlPFC were found in the FEF including 8Av and 8Ad.
claims.source: Laterally, axonal projections were found in the FEF including 8Av (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B and C) and 8Ad (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-D.

claims.claim: Dense axonal fibers from vlPFC were found in the dorsal prefrontal cortex, including area 8Bd, 8Bm, 8Bs, 46d, and 9d.
claims.source: Dorsally, there were dense axonal fibers in the dorsal prefrontal cortex, including area 8Bd (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E, F and G), 8Bm (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E), 8Bs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E), 46d (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E, H and I), and 9d (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E, J and K).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 2E-K.

claims.claim: The 8Bd and 46d received relatively more innervation from vlPFC compared with 9d, 8Bs, and 8Bm.
claims.source: The 8Bd and 46d received relatively more innervation compared with 9d, 8Bs, and 8Bm (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: Scattered axon fibers from vlPFC were visible in area F5, F7, and F2 of the premotor cortex.
claims.source: On the medial surface of the brain, scattered axon fibers were visible in area F5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L and M), F7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L and N), and F2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L) of the premotor cortex.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 2L-N.

claims.claim: The axons from vlPFC within the premotor cortex exhibited a gradient pattern with the largest axon distribution along the anterior part.
claims.source: The axons with the premotor cortex exhibited a gradient pattern with the largest axon distribution along the anterior part (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2L.

claims.claim: Axons from vlPFC were noted in the precentral opercular area (PrCO) and medial prefrontal area (mainly in 10mr).
claims.source: In addition, axons were noted in the precentral opercular area (PrCO) and medial prefrontal area (mainly in 10mr) (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The projections from vlPFC anchored in the prefrontal cortex formed isolated clusters.
claims.source: Interestingly, the projections anchored in the prefrontal cortex of these axonal fibers formed isolated clusters (Figure 4F and H, indicated by arrows).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4F and H.

claims.claim: The z-axis extent of axonal clusters from vlPFC was ranging from 1.2 mm to 3.8 mm (2.24 ± 0.80 mm).
claims.source: The z-axis extent of axonal clusters was ranging from 1.2 mm to 3.8 mm (2.24 ± 0.80 mm) (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, quantitative measurements, and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Rich connections from vlPFC were observed in the temporal lobe, predominantly in caudal lateral (CL), caudal (CPB), and rostral (RPB) portions of parabelt region of the auditory cortex.
claims.source: Beyond the frontal lobe, rich connections were observed in the temporal lobe (Figure 3), predominantly in caudal lateral (CL), caudal (CPB), and rostral (RPB) portions of parabelt region of the auditory cortex; anterior TE (TEa), medial TE (TEm), superior temporal polysensory area (STP, correspond to areas PGa and TPO), IPa and TAa of the dorsal bank/ventral bank/fundus of the superior temporal sulcus (STSd/v/f) (Figure 3C); medial superior temporal area (MST), floor of superior temporal area (FST), anteroventral TE (TEav), anterodorsal TE (TEad), and area TEO of superior temporal area.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 3 and Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The vlPFC sends axons to limbic regions, mainly in 24 a, 24 a', 24b, 24b', and 24 c of anterior cingulate areas (ACC).
claims.source: The vlPFC also sends axons to limbic regions, mainly in 24 a, 24 a', 24b, 24b',and 24 c of anterior cingulate areas (ACC) (Figure 3C); area TF of parahippocampal cortex (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Relatively weak projections from vlPFC were observed in the dorsal subdivision of lateral intraparietal area (LIPd); 7 a and 7b of inferior parietal lobule areas; secondary somatosensory area (SII) and parietal operculum (7op) of the parietal cortex.
claims.source: Relatively weak projections were observed in the dorsal subdivision of lateral intraparietal area (LIPd); 7 a and 7b of inferior parietal lobule areas; secondary somatosensory area (SII) and parietal operculum (7op) of the parietal cortex (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Sparsely labeled axons from vlPFC were found in the granular insula (Ig) and lateral agranular insula (Ial) area.
claims.source: There were some sparsely labeled axons in the granular insula (Ig) and lateral agranular insula (Ial) area (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Traveling axonal bundles from vlPFC were found in the corpus callosum, anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC), and anchored into the MD thalamus.
claims.source: In white matter, traveling axonal bundles were found in the corpus callosum, anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A, B), and anchored into the MD thalamus (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C, D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 4A-D.

claims.claim: Axon clusters from vlPFC were observed in the medial and caudal parts of caudate.
claims.source: Subcortically, axon clusters were observed in the medial (Figure 4—figure supplement 4F, G) and caudal (Figure 4—figure supplement 4H) parts of caudate.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 4F-H.

claims.claim: Axons in MD and caudate from vlPFC were thinner than those in the ALIC.
claims.source: High resolution confocal images revealed that axons in MD (Figure 4—figure supplement 4D) and caudate (Figure 4—figure supplement 4J) were thinner than those in the ALIC (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 4B, D, and J.

claims.claim: Labeled axons from vlPFC were found extending to the parvicellular part of accessory basal nucleus of amygdala (ABpc), reticulate and compacta parts of substantia nigra (SNr/c), claustrum and subthalamic nucleus (STN).
claims.source: Furthermore, the labeled axons were found extending to the parvicellular part of accessory basal nucleus of amygdala (ABpc), reticulate and compacta parts of substantia nigra (SNr/c), claustrum and subthalamic nucleus (STN) (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The Dice coefficients and Pearson coefficients between GFP projection and probabilistic tract were higher in dense projection regions, especially for the vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract.
claims.source: GFP projection and probabilistic tract were plotted with the Dice coefficients and Pearson coefficients (R) along the anterior-posterior axis of the whole macaque brain. The Dice coefficients and Pearson coefficients were higher in dense projection regions, especially for the vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 6A.

claims.claim: The dMRI-derived tracts largely overlapped with the axonal bundles shown in STP images for the vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract.
claims.source: Upon visual comparison, the dMRI-derived tracts largely overlapped with the axonal bundles shown in STP images (Figure 6B and C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 6B and C.

claims.claim: For all slices along vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract, consistent and significant correlations were observed between STP and dMRI modalities (R = 0.4624 ± 0.0922; Dice = 0.4312 ± 0.0861).
claims.source: For all slices (spaced by 500 μm) along vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract, we observed consistent and significant correlations between these two modalities (R = 0.4624 ± 0.0922; Dice = 0.4312 ± 0.0861).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and quantitative statistical measures.

claims.claim: The inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF) in macaques is a long-ranged bowtie-shaped tract as illustrated by diffusion tractography.
claims.source: As illustrated by diffusion tractography, the inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF) in macaques is a long-ranged bowtie-shaped tract (Figure 7A), showing traveling course similar to humans.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The frontal stem of IFOF spread to form a thin sheet, and its temporal stem narrowed in coronal section, mainly gathered at the external capsule.
claims.source: The frontal stem of IFOF spread to form a thin sheet, and its temporal stem narrowed in coronal section, mainly gathered at the external capsule.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the IFOF anatomy.

claims.claim: The posterior part of vlPFC axonal projections apparently ends at the middle superior temporal region, far from the occipital lobe.
claims.source: The intersection between IFOF and axonal projections of vlPFC was shown in a common 3D space of diffusion tractography in Figure 7B, whereby the posterior part of vlPFC axonal projections apparently ends at the middle superior temporal region, far from the occipital lobe.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7B.

claims.claim: The Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficient between the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome was 0.0397 and 0.0535 in 3D space for two dMRI data sets, indicating that only a small fraction of the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome overlapped.
claims.source: To quantify the spatial correspondence between the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome, the Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficient was calculated in a shared common 3D space after co-registration. It was 0.0397 and 0.0535 in 3D space for two dMRI data sets, indicating that only a small fraction of the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome overlapped (mainly in the front half of the brain, Figure 7).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, quantitative measurements, and reference to Figure 7.

claims.claim: The anterior part of the vlPFC axonal projections shown by STP tomography largely overlapped with the dMRI-derived IFOF tracts in frontal whiter matter, external capsule, claustrum, and extreme capsule.
claims.source: The anterior part of the vlPFC axonal projections shown by STP tomography largely overlapped with the dMRI-derived IFOF tracts in frontal whiter matter (Figure 7D), external capsule (Figure 7E), claustrum (Figure 7E and F), and extreme capsule (Figure 7F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 7D-F.

claims.claim: The posterior part of dMRI-derived IFOF tract passed through temporal white matter, whereas the posterior part of fiber projections of vlPFC sent no axons to this region.
claims.source: Meanwhile, the posterior part of dMRI-derived IFOF tract passed through temporal white matter (Figure 7G), whereas the posterior part of fiber projections of vlPFC sent no axons to this region (Figure 7G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7G.

claims.claim: The dMRI-derived SLFIII substantially overlapped with the vlPFC axonal projections in frontal and parietal whiter matter along the whole trajectory.
claims.source: Unlike the IFOF in which the results of diffusion tractography mainly overlapped with those of viral tracing in the anterior part (Figure 7), the dMRI-derived SLFIII substantially overlapped with the vlPFC axonal projections in frontal and parietal whiter matter along the whole trajectory (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficients between the SLFIII derived from diffusion tractography and the parietal branch of vlPFC projections identified from viral tracing showed markedly high overlap (r = 0.2603 and 0.2175).
claims.source: Similarly, we calculated the Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficients between the SLFIII derived from diffusion tractography and the parietal branch of vlPFC projections identified from viral tracing in two brain samples, as showed markedly high overlap (r = 0.2603 and 0.2175).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and quantitative measurements.

claims.claim: STP tomography was customized for whole-brain imaging of the macaque monkey at submicron resolution.
claims.source: We customized STP tomography for whole-brain imaging of the macaque monkey at submicron resolution and accomplished brain-wide 3D reconstruction of axonal connectome, thanks to prominent characteristics of STP tomography including free of tissue distortions, no need for section-to-section alignment, and high-resolution image sets readily warped in 3D space (Amato et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and a citation to Amato et al., 2016.

claims.claim: STP tomography has prominent characteristics including free of tissue distortions, no need for section-to-section alignment, and high-resolution image sets readily warped in 3D space.
claims.source: We customized STP tomography for whole-brain imaging of the macaque monkey at submicron resolution and accomplished brain-wide 3D reconstruction of axonal connectome, thanks to prominent characteristics of STP tomography including free of tissue distortions, no need for section-to-section alignment, and high-resolution image sets readily warped in 3D space (Amato et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and a citation to Amato et al., 2016.

claims.claim: A CaMKIIα promoter carried by lentivirus was able to target excitatory neurons with optogenetic proteins in the macaque brain.
claims.source: Previous studies have demonstrated that a CaMKIIα promoter carried by lentivirus was able to target excitatory neurons with optogenetic proteins in the macaque brain (Han et al., 2009), and a TH promoter carried by AAV selectively targeted dopamine neurons (Stauffer et al., 2016).

results.result: VSV-ΔG viral vector testing in macaque brain showed rapid GFP expression in neuronal cell bodies within 5 days but only labeled proximal neurites without long-range axonal fibers. Extended infection time (~1 month) caused widespread axon loss, neuronal cell death, and apoptotic morphological changes including membrane blebbing, demonstrating fatal neurotoxicity.
results.evaluation: Claims C18-C23 provide consistent experimental evidence from multiple timepoints showing VSV-ΔG's limitations for long-range tracing. The short-term (5 days) and long-term (~1 month) observations are well-documented with figure references, and the apoptotic markers (membrane blebbing) provide mechanistic support for the neurotoxicity conclusion.

results.result: Lenti-Ubic-GFP exhibited stable expression in cell soma for up to 9 months but resulted in sparse labeling of GFP-positive axons.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C25 are supported by experimental observations with figure references (Figure 2C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3). The long-term stability (9 months) is clearly demonstrated, though the sparse axonal labeling limits its utility for comprehensive tract tracing.

results.result: AAV2/9-CaMKIIa-Tau-GFP demonstrated superior performance for long-range axonal tracing, with clear visualization of fiber bundles over several centimeters at 6 weeks post-injection, neuron-specific labeling, and significantly higher axonal fiber density compared to both Lentivirus (P<0.001) and VSV-ΔG (P<0.001).
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C31 provide comprehensive evidence including visualization data, cell-type specificity validation (NeuN+/GFAP-), comparative signal intensity analysis, and statistical comparisons. The P-values are reported and the conclusion that AAV2/9 is optimal for long-range tracing is well-supported by converging evidence.

results.result: The AAV injection site in vlPFC was precisely localized to cortical gray matter spanning areas 45, 12l, and 44, with immunofluorescent validation confirming that labeled neurons were CaMKIIa-positive and GABA-negative, indicating specific targeting of glutamate excitatory neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C33 are supported by STP imaging validation and immunofluorescent staining with appropriate markers. The dual-marker approach (positive for excitatory marker, negative for inhibitory marker) provides strong evidence for cell-type specificity.

results.result: Brain-wide mapping of vlPFC excitatory projections revealed extensive connectivity to frontal, temporal, and limbic regions with no projections to the occipital lobe. Within the frontal lobe, the strongest innervation was to OFC area 12m, with dense projections to dorsal prefrontal cortex (8Bd, 46d) and gradient patterns in premotor cortex. Projections formed isolated clusters with z-axis extent of 1.2-3.8 mm (2.24±0.80 mm). Rich temporal lobe connections were observed in auditory cortex and superior temporal sulcus regions, with additional projections to limbic regions (ACC), subcortical structures (caudate, MD thalamus via ALIC), and sparse projections to parietal and insular cortices.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C52 provide detailed anatomical mapping with extensive figure references and quantitative measurements. The absence of occipital projections is a key negative finding that is clearly stated. The hierarchical organization of projection strengths and the quantification of cluster dimensions add rigor. The comprehensive coverage across multiple brain regions with consistent documentation supports the overall projectome characterization.

results.result: Quantitative comparison of vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract showed higher Dice and Pearson coefficients in dense projection regions, with dMRI-derived tracts largely overlapping with STP axonal bundles. Consistent and significant correlations were observed across all slices (R=0.4624±0.0922; Dice=0.4312±0.0861).
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C55 provide quantitative validation with appropriate statistical measures (Dice coefficients and Pearson correlations). The reported values with standard deviations indicate proper statistical analysis. The visual and quantitative agreement between modalities for this specific tract is well-documented.

results.result: The IFOF in macaques was reconstructed as a long-ranged bowtie-shaped tract by diffusion tractography. However, comparison with viral tracing revealed that vlPFC axonal projections ended at the middle superior temporal region without reaching the occipital lobe. The Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficient was only 0.0397-0.0535, indicating minimal spatial correspondence. While the anterior portions overlapped in frontal white matter, external capsule, claustrum, and extreme capsule, the posterior dMRI-derived IFOF tract passed through temporal white matter where no vlPFC axons were detected.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C61 present a major finding challenging the existence of direct vlPFC-to-occipital connections via IFOF. The evidence is strong: quantitative overlap coefficients are very low, and the spatial mismatch in posterior regions is clearly documented with figure references. This represents a critical validation of dMRI tractography limitations.

results.result: The dMRI-derived SLFIII showed substantial overlap with vlPFC axonal projections in frontal and parietal white matter along the entire trajectory, with Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficients of 0.2603 and 0.2175, indicating markedly higher correspondence than IFOF.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C63 provide a positive control comparison showing that dMRI tractography can accurately reconstruct some pathways. The overlap coefficients are 5-7 times higher than for IFOF, and the whole-trajectory agreement contrasts with the anterior-only overlap seen for IFOF. This strengthens the conclusion that the IFOF discrepancy is not due to general dMRI failure.

results.result: STP tomography was customized for whole-brain imaging of macaque monkey at submicron resolution, with characteristics including freedom from tissue distortions, no need for section-to-section alignment, and high-resolution image sets readily warped in 3D space.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C65 describe the technical capabilities of the STP system with citation support (Amato et al., 2016). The advantages listed are inherent to the STP approach and are demonstrated throughout the manuscript with the successful whole-brain imaging results.

results.result: Immunofluorescent staining with CaMKIIα and GABA antibodies confirmed that GFP was specifically expressed in excitatory neurons.
results.evaluation: Claim C68 is supported by experimental validation using appropriate markers for excitatory (CaMKIIα) and inhibitory (GABA) neurons. This validation is critical for interpreting the projectome as specifically representing excitatory connections.

results.result: The excitatory projection pattern of vlPFC was compatible with previous chemical tracer studies and markedly similar to the CoCoMac database, with some previously unreported or unspecified projections to PFCol, PFCdm, PFCdl, PFCoi, PFCm, PMCvl, amygdala, and SII.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C70 provide important validation by comparing current results with established databases and prior studies. The general agreement with CoCoMac and cited tracer studies supports the validity of the AAV-based approach, while noting some novel findings.

results.result: GFP-labeled axonal density maps significantly overlapped with dMRI-derived probabilistic maps throughout the traveling course and demonstrated comparable connectivity strengths and patterns.
results.evaluation: Claim C86 summarizes the general agreement between STP and dMRI modalities. This is supported by the quantitative analyses presented in other claims (C53-C55, C62-C63), though the degree of agreement varies by tract.

results.result: Ex-vivo tractography showed fiber connections between frontal and occipital lobes matching the IFOF trajectory in humans, but anterograde AAV tracing revealed that vlPFC fiber projections passed through external capsule, claustrum, and extreme capsule to anchor at the middle superior temporal region without reaching the occipital lobe.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C93 highlight the key discrepancy between dMRI tractography and viral tracing for the IFOF. The use of the same ROI seeds as prior studies (Barrett et al., 2020; Feng et al., 2017) strengthens the comparison. The finding that AAV tracing (without trans-synaptic capability) shows no occipital projections is a critical result.

results.result: The study presents a detailed excitatory connectivity projection map from vlPFC to the entire macaque brain and demonstrates a broadly applicable roadmap for integrating 3D STP tomography with diffusion tractography for mesoscopic mapping of brain circuits in primates.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C96 summarize the main contributions of the study. The detailed projectome is well-documented throughout the results, and the methodological integration of STP and dMRI with quantitative validation represents a significant technical advance.

results.result: The customized STP tomography system integrated a two-photon microscope with a vibratome, with XYZ stage range of 50×60×70 mm, acquiring high-resolution (0.95 μm/pixel) serial 2D images at 200 μm z-intervals. Scanning time was 1.629 s per 1024×1024 pixel field-of-view, resulting in ~1 month continuous scanning and ~5 TB data per brain.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C102 provide detailed technical specifications of the STP system with figure references. The specifications are internally consistent and the data volume and scanning time are reasonable given the resolution and brain size.

results.result: A machine learning algorithm was used to segment GFP-labeled axonal fibers and remove lipofuscin background, requiring ~1.5 months computational time per brain, with classifier performance achieving F-score of 94.41±1.99%.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C105 describe the image analysis pipeline with appropriate citations (Arganda-Carreras et al., 2017; Gehrlach et al., 2020). The F-score indicates good classifier performance, though details about the training set size and validation approach are limited.

results.result: Diffusion images achieved SNRs of 48.34±8.50 (b=0) and 23.13±2.05 (b=4000), meeting the recommended threshold of SNR>20 for b=0 images to obtain relatively unbiased FA measures.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C107 provide quality control metrics for the dMRI data with citation to established guidelines (Mukherjee et al., 2008). The SNR values are appropriate for the high b-value used (4000 s/mm²) in ex-vivo imaging.

results.result: The vlPFC spans Brodmann's Areas 44, 45a/b, 46v/f, and 12r/l, is central to language, objective memory, and decision-making functions, and its abnormalities are associated with deficits in cognitive flexibility.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 provide background context about vlPFC with appropriate citations. These are established facts from prior literature rather than new findings from this study.

results.result: Histological neural tracing remains the most reliable method for surveying myelinated axons and serves as the gold standard for validating diffusion tractography, though diffusion tractography represents the only methodology for inferring anatomical connections in living brains despite being an indirect observation with limited resolution and accuracy.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C8 establish the methodological context with extensive citations. These represent consensus views in the field about the complementary strengths and limitations of histological tracing versus diffusion tractography.

results.result: The IFOF supposedly connects vlPFC and medial OFC to the occipital lobe through the ventral external capsule, with anatomy confirmed by micro-dissection and diffusion MRI studies in humans, but axonal tracing studies in macaques have yielded conflicting results, with some failing to reveal the IFOF while others reported sparse fronto-occipital connections.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C14 establish the controversy about IFOF existence in macaques with appropriate citations. This background motivates the current study's investigation of this question using combined viral tracing and dMRI.

results.result: The study established a comprehensive brain-wide excitatory projectome of vlPFC using viral-based genetic tracing with STP tomography and performed ex vivo dMRI scans at 11.7T for comparison.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C17 describe the overall study design and methodology. The approach is clearly documented with figure references and represents a valid experimental strategy for addressing the research questions.

results.result: Prior studies demonstrated that CaMKIIα promoter in lentivirus targets excitatory neurons in macaque brain, TH promoter in AAV targets dopamine neurons, and various viral vectors have distinct properties. VSV-G failed to label transsynaptic cells at distant areas, lentivirus has large genetic capacity (~10 Kb), and AAV has minimal toxicity with high transfection efficiency but limited packaging capacity (~4.8 Kb). AAV2 is widely used and effectively transfects primate neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C67, C71-C80 provide literature context about viral vector properties with appropriate citations. These establish the rationale for testing different vectors and inform the interpretation of results.

results.result: AAV2/9 vector was more suitable for long-range axonal fiber tracing, while VSV-ΔG was suitable for rapid gene expression and lentivirus for long-term gene expression in macaques.
results.evaluation: Claim C81 summarizes the comparative viral vector findings. This conclusion is well-supported by the experimental data in claims C18-C30 showing the distinct temporal and spatial characteristics of each vector.

results.result: Prior cross-modality comparison studies constructed connectivity matrices using dMRI tractography and tracer-injection tracing in mice and monkeys, with varying correlative evidence (r=0.21 to r=0.59). results.evaluation: Claims C82-C85 provide context about prior validation studies with appropriate citations. The range of reported correlations (r=0.21-0.59) highlights the variability in dMRI-tracer agreement and motivates the need for more detailed spatial validation.
